correctness.rationale: Direct graph construction over F_2^4 gives 30 vertices, 45 edges, girth eight, and diameter four. The exact backwards winning recurrence (proved by cop-then-robber quantifier induction) exhausts 30 states per cop multiset, including repeated cop locations and pass moves. With one and two cops, the winning-position masks stabilize at horizons one and two respectively without any all-robber initial state; with three cops exactly seventy of 4,960 start multisets win by turn three and none by turn two. An independent-in-implementation complement recursion reproduces the same 70 start states and all counts. All seventy are precisely the 35 projective point triples, 15 line pencils, and 20 regulus triples. A separate two-ball covering argument proves that no three-cop start wins in two rounds. Actual executable files verify_game.py and verify_dual.py and their generated outputs are included.

originality.rationale: The result is the precise three-round capture time and all optimal unordered triple placements for the thirty-vertex Tutte–Coxeter incidence graph, not the familiar girth-degree cop-number lower bound. Prior papers cover cop-number inequalities for design graphs, general capture-time theory, or hypercube capture time; none of the accessible material implies the 70-start geometry. Published records about Vietoris–Rips and other complexes of the same graph use different objects and parameters. Targeted searches found no exact equivalent. The full design-paper publisher text was not available and unindexed work remains a residual risk.
residual_risks: The 2012 Bonato–Burgess complete article was not available for full-document inspection; an attempted institutional-access request required human input.
Unindexed finite calculations or equivalent cop-placement classifications could exist under other terminology.

value.rationale: The Tutte–Coxeter graph is the classical smallest cubic girth-eight cage and naturally tests pursuit on a sparse highly symmetric incidence graph. The capture-time invariant and complete characterization of all fastest feasible initial configurations answer a natural deployment question. The precise 35 projective lines, 15 point pencils, and 20 reguli are geometric structural categories, not arbitrary hand-picked subsets; the result is exact for every three-cop starting placement rather than a partial census. The proof distinguishes a known lower bound on cop count from new optimal-time geometry. It makes no unsupported claim of a general theorem for larger designs.
